subject: Private deployment IP airlock — outbound restrictions & permit-listing
messages:
From: Sana Patel <sana.patel@bluepeak.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: BluePeak Network Team <netops@bluepeak.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment IP airlock — outbound restrictions & permit-listing

Jonas,

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. As we prepare to move the BluePeak private deployment into staging, our security team asked for a definitive set of outbound controls we need to implement on our side (firewall rules, NAT choices, and any hostname/IP allowlisting). We attached our current topology for reference.

Primary asks from NetOps & SecOps:
- A single canonical list of destination IP ranges and ports that must be allowlisted for the Redwood control plane (including health checks, telemetry, and management APIs).
- Whether model artifacts (weights/quantized bundles) are pulled from fixed endpoints (and IPs) or from CDN/S3 hostnames that may change IPs frequently. If the latter, what are the recommended mitigation patterns?
- Clarify DNS behavior: do you require egress to public DNS resolvers, or can we force egress DNS to our internal resolvers and still function?
- TLS/inspection guidance: we plan to enforce TLS inspection at the perimeter for outbound flows. Does Redwood support certificate validation / client cert pinning, or will TLS interception break runtime connectivity?
- Recommended firewall rule snippets we can give to our infra team (Palo Alto + iptables examples) for quick implementation.

We would like to implement a tight policy in staging by Wednesday; can you provide a recommended allowlist + short runbook? I attached our topology (bp-infra-topology-20261005.png).

Thanks,
Sana Patel
Security Program Manager | BluePeak Analytics
Attachments: bp-infra-topology-20261005.png
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana.patel@bluepeak.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment IP airlock — outbound restrictions & permit-listing

Hi Sana — thanks for the clear list. Summarizing the practical constraints and recommended options below so your NetOps team can pick the approach that best matches BluePeak policy. Attaching a compact CSV with the primary IP ranges and a one-page doc with rule examples (redwood-ip-list-20261005.csv; bp-egress-requirements-20261005.docx).

Quick answers up-front:
1) Control plane management/telemetry: require allowlist to our control plane egress IP ranges (see CSV). Ports: 443 (HTTPS) primarily, and 10250 for health-check tunnels on dedicated setups only.
2) Model artifacts: Redwood serves model assets via signed HTTPS URLs on CDN-backed buckets. IPs may change — we provide two mitigations:
   a) Static egress NAT: you provide a fixed outbound IP (or small range) and allow DNS/HTTPS to the artifact hostnames; we recommend pinning by hostname + TLS cert validation.
   b) Proxy/NAT + egress IPs from Redwood: if you prefer, we can arrange a managed egress NAT (static IPs) as part of the Dedicated/Private contract for model fetches.
3) DNS: we support internal resolvers (you can force DNS to your resolvers). However, if you block DNS to public resolvers, ensure your resolver can resolve the CDN hostnames and that TLS cert validation remains intact.
4) TLS interception: we do not recommend TLS interception for connections carrying model artifacts or control-plane auth tokens. Intercepting TLS will break certificate validation and may break mutual auth in some customer-managed mTLS flows. If inspection is mandatory, consider terminating at an internal proxy (validate, then re-establish TLS to Redwood) and configure certificate pinning/expected CNs at the proxy.

Recommended rule set (concise):
- Outbound: allow TCP/443 to hostnames: *.redwood-inference.com, artifacts.redwood-cdn.com, telemetry.redwood-inference.com; but if your policy cannot operate on hostnames, allow destination IPs in attached CSV (redwood-ip-list-20261005.csv).
- DNS: allow outbound to your resolver + allowlist egress to external resolvers if the internal resolver needs upstream.
- Fallback: allow ephemeral ranges used by large cloud CDNs (we list common CDN prefixes in the doc) if you cannot pin exact IPs.

Firewall snippets (in full doc) include:
- Palo Alto: source zone = private, dest zone = internet, application = ssl, URL category = custom allowlist of redwood hostnames, service = service-tcp-443.
- iptables example (Linux NAT gateway):
  iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d <redwood-ip> --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
  iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP

Operational notes:
- Caching: enable an artifact cache/proxy in your perimeter to reduce model download frequency. Signed URLs have short TTLs, so the cache needs to revalidate via HTTPS.
- Client IP preservation: if you NAT through a shared egress, Redwood will see the NAT IP; we can pass X-Forwarded-For-like headers over the control channel for audit purposes when configured with a mutual TLS tunnel.

Next steps:
- Confirm whether BluePeak will provide static egress IP(s) or if you want Redwood-managed egress.
- We will finalize the CSV with a published range and handoff the Palo Alto + iptables snippets for your ops playbook.

Jonas Weber
Head of Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-ip-list-20261005.csv, bp-egress-requirements-20261005.docx
From: BluePeak Network Team <netops@bluepeak.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@bluepeak.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment IP airlock — outbound restrictions & permit-listing

Jonas / team — quick clarification from NetOps:

1) TLS interception: our corporate policy mandates TLS inspection for outbound flows by default. We can make exceptions, but that requires an explicit justification and a compensating control. If we cannot avoid inspection, will the approach you recommended (terminate + re-establish at internal proxy) maintain session fidelity for health checks and streaming telemetry?

2) Model artifact IP churn: we prefer to avoid allowing broad CDN ranges. Can Redwood provide a stable hostname that resolves to a small, documented set of IPs for the artifact endpoints used during initial deploys? If not, what is the expected cadence of IP changes?

3) If we provide a single static NAT IP for your services to pull from, will Redwood honor that in ACLs for callbacks (for audit/whitelisting) and for license-management callbacks?

Also, please confirm how long the control plane IP list in the CSV is expected to remain valid before any scheduled rotation.

Thanks,
BluePeak NetOps
Attachments: none

Subject: Re: Private deployment IP airlock — outbound restrictions & permit-listing

Thanks for the follow-ups — answers inline and a short final recommendation below.

1) TLS inspection: If BluePeak must inspect TLS at the perimeter, the supported pattern is: terminate TLS at your proxy, perform inspection, and then re-establish TLS to Redwood endpoints. For streaming telemetry we recommend configuring the proxy to allow passthrough for websocket/HTTP2 health streams where possible; otherwise, re-originating TLS with full cert validation preserves connectivity but you will no longer have end-to-end cert validation from the cluster to Redwood. As a compensating control, enable mutual TLS for control-plane tunnels so authentication is independent of TLS inspection.

2) Artifact IP stability: We can offer a deployment-window guarantee: for the initial staging rollout we will publish a short-lived stable set of IP addresses for artifacts (valid for 14 days) and a DNS name that resolves to those IPs. Longer-term, artifacts are served via CDN and IPs can change; for production we recommend either (a) static egress NAT from BluePeak, or (b) an internal artifact cache/proxy that you control. We will provide a weekly change log with any IP rotations and at least 48 hours notice for non-emergency changes.

3) Static NAT & callbacks: Yes — if you provide a static egress IP, we will accept that as a whitelisted source for callbacks and license-management callbacks. We'll add the IP to our allowlist for audit logging and per-deal ACLs.

Control plane IP rotation policy: published CSV will roll monthly by default; emergency rotations may happen with 48 hours notice. We'll include a signed manifest for each CSV so your automation can validate changes.

Final recommended immediate rule set for staging (minimal):
- Allow outbound TCP/443 from private subnet(s) to the following hostnames: telemetry.redwood-inference.com, control.redwood-inference.com, artifacts-staging.redwood-inference.com
- Allow outbound DNS to your internal resolver and allowlist your resolver to reach public upstream if needed.
- BLOCK outbound to wide CDN ranges unless explicitly allowed.
- If TLS inspection is enforced, configure a proxy that re-establishes TLS and configure mTLS for the control plane tunnel (we will provide certs and instructions).

I will share the signed CSV and the staging artifact IP list by EOD; if BluePeak confirms you will provide a single static NAT IP, we will add that IP to the per-deal ACL and provide the patch for your firewall team.

Next actions:
- BluePeak to confirm static NAT vs Redwood-managed egress.
- BluePeak to confirm TLS inspection exception or proxy config timeline.
- Redwood to publish signed CSV and staging artifact IPs (attached).

Jonas Weber
Head of Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
